cohort: The study included 100 pregnant women, equally divided into two groups: those aged 19 years or less and those aged 30 years or more, recruited at a tertiary care hospital.
finding: The study found a higher incidence of eclampsia in pregnant women aged >=30 years and, though not statistically significant, more neonatal deaths and low birth weights in women aged <=19 years, with no significant differences in marital status, rural residency, hemoglobin levels, or cesarean delivery rates between the age groups.
mod_finding: The study found no significant differences in cesarean delivery rates between pregnant women aged <=19 and those aged >=30 years.
birth_weight: N/A (only incidence of low birth weight was reported)
